newsitem.title: USA: Criminal charges filed in N.J. muni kickback case.
newsitem.headline: Criminal charges filed in N.J. muni kickback case.

text.p: The U.S. Attorneys Office in Newark said Thursday it indicted the former Treasurer of Essex County, N.J., in connection with an alleged scheme to receive kickbacks in exchange for steering muni business to two firms.
The charges, filed against Joseph Galluzzi of Springfield, came as the Securities and Exchange Commission filed a companion case against Galluzzi alleging violations of U.S. securities laws.

The criminal charges allege Galluzzi received $170,000 in kickbacks from First Fidelity Securities, now a unit of First Union Corp, and $15,000 from AG Edwards & Co in Newark, a unit of AG Edwards Inc.

A spokesman for First Union, Paul Levine, said the firm had no comment on either the US Attorneys allegations, or the charges brought by the SEC. A spokesman for AG Edwards said the firm did not yet have a statement.
First Fidelity, without admitting or denying guilt, already settled allegations tied to the matter by paying penalties and fees totalling nearly $2.3 million.

Galluzzi, who was not arrested, could not immediately be reached for comment. He was charged with mail fraud, acceptance of corrupt payments and use of a facility in interstate commerce to receive illegal benefits.
